newsitem.title: USA: MergeGlobal sees strong air cargo growth thro' 2002.
newsitem.headline: MergeGlobal sees strong air cargo growth thro' 2002.

text.p: World air cargo traffic will grow at a compounded annual average of 7.1 percent for the next six years, slightly slower than the 7.3 percent growth rate experienced during the past six years, the MergeGloba air cargo consultancy said.
MergeGlobal, a leading U.S. consultancy, forecast that U.S. import/export traffic to/from all regions will increase by 7.3 percent.

In its 1997 market forecast, MergeGlobal said the strongest growth of all major markets will occur in the intra-Asia market, where traffic will grow by 9.5 percent annually, not as fast as the 13.7 percent rate experienced from 1990-96.

"Lingering problems in Japan's property and banking sectors, political instability in Indonesia and the uncertain prospects for economic reform in China and India are three big reasons why future growth may be slower than historical," the MergeGlobal forecast said.
Positive forces for growth include further liberalization of the Chinese and Indian economy and the continuing shift of production capacity from North Asia to Southeast Asia.
In specific markets, U.S.-Southeast Asia traffic will grow by nine percent, down from 13.6 percent during 1990-96. it added.
Western Europe-Asia traffic will rise by 7.8 percent annually.

U.S.-Western Europe traffic will grow at a forecast rate of 5.8 percent, down from 6.4 percent for 1990-96. US exports are impected to grow by 7.3 percent a year, an increase over the 5.3 percent growth of the past six years, but import traffic will grow by 5.4 percent, compared by 1990-96 annual growth of 6.5 percent.
There will be some moderation in the growth of U.S.-Latin American air freight, said MergeGlobal.

One of the hotter growth sectors during 1990-96 at 7.6 percent, U.S.-Latin American traffic is expected to grow by only six percent through 2002 due to moderating growth in Latin American air exports to the US.

Smaller air freight markets will experience strong growth, it said. Europe-South America traffic will grow at a compound annual rate of 12.9 percent. Air cargo traffic between the U.S. and NAFTA countries (Mexico and Canada) will grow at 9.6 percent per year.
Air exports from the Commonwealth of Independent States to the U.S. will grow at a 10.9 percent rate, up from 7.2 percent annual growth during the 1990-96 period.
MergeGlobal forecast intra-Europe traffic to grow at 3.8 percent a year, up from 3.3 percent in 1990-96. -Air Cargo Newsroom Tel +44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
